 NEA makes arrangements to ensure smooth power supply during festivals
 TRN Online 
 Sun, 8 November 2026 
 Share 
 Change Font Sizes: 
 TRN Online 
 Share: 
 Sun, 8 November 2026 
 By A Staff Reporter 
 Kathmandu, Nov. 8:  The Nepal Electricity Authority (NEA) has made special arrangements to ensure a reliable, regular and quality power supply to consumers during the Tihar and Chhath festivals.
 To prevent power disruptions during Tihar, the festival of lights, the authority has made arrangements to keep electricity generation, transmission and distribution systems fully operational and keep technical staff standby round the clock.
 A meeting of the authority’s senior management team, chaired by managing director Dirghayu Kumar Shrestha, was held to discuss preparations for the smooth operation of the power system and management of potential challenges during the festivals.
 Similarly, a joint virtual meeting was held with chiefs of the provincial and provincial division offices under the Load Dispatch Centre (LDC), Grid Operation Department, and Distribution and Customer Service Directorate.
 The meeting discussed power supply management, system monitoring and mobilisation of the required workforce.
 MD Shrestha directed the chiefs of concerned offices to make all necessary arrangements to prevent disruptions to power supply throughout the festive period. 
 He also instructed them to keep technical teams on standby to carry out immediate repairs and restore services in the event of any disruption.
 Likewise, the concerned offices have been directed to complete pending inspection and maintenance works on transmission lines and distribution systems promptly to minimise possible disruptions.
 The office chiefs have also been instructed to ensure that calls received through the 'No Light' service are answered regularly and that consumer complaints related to power supply are addressed promptly and effectively, said the NEA. According to MD Shrestha, the peak electricity demand on the evening of Laxmi Puja during Tihar is estimated at around 1,700 megawatts. 
 He said domestic generation alone would be sufficient to meet the demand.
 Electricity generation during the period is projected to reach around 2,500 megawatts. 
 As domestic production is expected to exceed internal demand, sufficient electricity will be available to ensure a smooth power supply, he said.
 The LDC, Grid Operation Department and distribution centres will maintain regular coordination to monitor electricity demand and supply throughout the festive period. 
 Necessary technical and managerial arrangements have also been made to identify potential problems in the system in time and address them immediately.
 Meanwhile, the authority has urged consumers to use electricity safely during Tihar and Chhath. 
 It has advised households to check the condition of electrical appliances and wiring, avoid using substandard electrical materials and seek assistance from qualified technicians rather than attempting to repair electrical leakage or faulty wires themselves.
 The NEA has also urged consumers to contact their nearest distribution centre or the concerned No Light service if they face any power supply problems or have complaints.
